MGTA 402.pre: MGTA 451 (minimum grade B-); MGTA 452 (minimum grade B-); MGTA 453 (minimum grade B-)
MGTA 402.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Business Analytics

MGTA 403.t: AI-Assisted Math and Programming for Business Analytics
MGTA 403.desc: Success in business analytics (aka data science for business) requires a solid foundation in mathematics, statistics, and programming. This course is designed to enhance students’ ability to solve math and programming challenges using AI tools like ChatGPT (Code Interpreter) and GitHub Co-Pilot X. This AI-assisted course will be the start of the students’ learning journey and will set students up to create analytical solutions to important business problems.
MGTA 403.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics students or instructor approval or department approval.

MGTA 414.desc: This course focuses on collecting, drawing inference, and making business decisions based on data. It will cover tools such as Python, APIs, and NLP to collect, manipulate, and analyze data from the web and other sources, with the objective of making students data-savvy and comfortable with deriving insights from real-world, large data sets. Students will be exposed to the power of clickstream analysis and the possibilities that can be unleashed from industrial applications of web data analytics.
MGTA 414.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics students or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 415.desc: Unstructured data such as text, images, and video are routinely collected by companies and other organizations. The complex nature and scale of data such as this requires specialized analytics frameworks. In this course, we discuss and use tools that empower decision makers to extract actionable information from unstructured data.
MGTA 415.pre: MGTA 452, and restricted to MS in business analytics students or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 444.desc: The framing of the solution approach is arguably the most important step in building a practical solution to a complex business problem. Should one do a statistical analysis, build a machine learning predictive model, a forecast, a simulation? What are we trying to understand or predict? What is the business objective? What are the deliverables? How will our results be evaluated? This course will give the students experience at framing a wide variety of business analytics problems.
MGTA 444.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program.

MGTA 451.t: Business Analytics in Marketing, Finance, and Operations
MGTA 451.desc: Business analytics projects should strive to create substantial value to an organization by solving impactful business problems. In this class, students will learn to identify business opportunities in the substantive areas of marketing, finance, and operations. Letter grades only.
MGTA 451.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 452.desc: This course aims to provide students with an introduction to data analytics in R where the emphasis is more on business “data” than “analytics.” The emphasis is on collecting, handling, manipulating, and summarizing large data sets. Case studies are used throughout the course.
MGTA 452.pre: MGTA 451 and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.
MGTA 452.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Business Analytics

MGTA 453.desc: This course is designed to help a business manager to use data to make good decisions in complex decision-making situations. Several analytical and econometric methods will be covered including decision analysis, regression analysis, optimization, and simulation.
MGTA 453.pre: MGTA 451 and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.
MGTA 453.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Business Analytics

MGTA 454.desc: Students will pursue their capstone experience as part of a team to solve practical business problems faced by companies. Each team will work as external consultants on a project to create value for a client company. Student may not receive credit for both MGTA 454 and MGTA 454A or MGTA 454B.
MGTA 454.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 454A.desc: Project-based course, in which students apply knowledge and methods acquired in their course work to a specific business analytics problem faced by a company. The project will be comprehensive in nature, allowing students to exhibit their acquired skills. Class meetings will be scheduled where teams will outline project goals, describe the available data and planned analyses, and present initial results. This course is part of a course series. An IP grade will be awarded at the end of the quarter. Final grade will not apply until the completion of MGTA 454B. Students may not receive credit for both MGTA 454A and MGTA 454.
MGTA 454A.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 454B.desc: Project-based course, in which students apply knowledge and methods acquired in their course work to a specific business analytics problem faced by a company. This is a continuation of MGTA 454A. Class meetings will be scheduled where teams will present their interim and final analysis results and outline how the partner company could use the project outcomes (e.g., a decision support tool) in decision-making. This course is part of a course series. Final grade will apply after the completion of MGTA 454B. Students may not receive credit for both MGTA 454 and MGTA 454A or MGTA 454B.
MGTA 454B.pre: MGTA 454A and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 455.desc: Many firms have extensive information about customers’ choices and how they respond to business initiatives. In this course, you will learn to leverage AI and machine learning to collect, analyze, and act on such customer data. The course is hands-on, uses real-world data, and will equip students with skills that produce immediate value on the job. Python, Radiant for Python, ChatGPT with Code Interpreter, and Co-Pilot are the key analytical tools used in the class. Letter grade only. Students may not earn credit for both MGTA 455 and MGTA 455R.
MGTA 455.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 455R.desc: Many firms have extensive information about customers’ choices and how they respond to business initiatives. In this course, you will learn to leverage AI and machine learning to collect, analyze, and act on such customer data. The course is hands-on, uses real-world data, and will equip students with skills that produce immediate value on the job. Python, Radiant for Python, ChatGPT with Code Interpreter, and Co-Pilot are the key analytical tools used in the class. Letter grade only. Students may not receive credit for both MGTA 455R and MGTA 455.
MGTA 455R.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 456.desc: This course focuses on improving the performance of production and service operations, as well as supply chains, through the combination of data and analytical tools including statistics, forecasting, and optimization. Students will learn to employ analytics in capacity and distribution facility planning and contracting; how to determine data collection requirements for dynamic management of inventory levels; and how to improve revenue management under demand learning.
MGTA 456.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 457.desc: A decision support system consists of decision model, data, and user interface. This course covers the R and Shiny programming and design skills to develop a DSS that addresses a manager’s decision-making needs.
MGTA 457.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.
MGTA 457.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Business Analytics

MGTA 458.desc: Students will learn to design and run experiments to guide policy and business decisions. They will learn to distinguish between a correlation and a causal effect and also to critically evaluate causal claims based on nonexperimental data. Letter grade only.
MGTA 458.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, and MGTA 453. Restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 459.desc: Decision making is difficult with scarce resources, inexact information, and conflicting stakeholder agendas (i.e., most of the time). Students will use advanced behavioral research to gain a competitive advantage, by improving their decisions and their understanding of how others decide.
MGTA 459.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.
MGTA 459.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Business Analytics

MGTA 460.desc: Many projects fail to produce valuable results, are over budget, or not finished on time. This course will teach students how to set and manage goals and expectations of the team and of the executive sponsors for business analytics projects.
MGTA 460.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 461.desc: A graduate course devoted to current methods for recommender systems, data mining, and predictive analytics.
MGTA 461.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Business Analytics

MGTA 462.desc: This course is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to manage large-scale and complex data for business applications. Students will learn how to handle large volumes of data through database systems and to use big data technologies to perform scalable analytics.
MGTA 462.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 463.desc: In this course students will learn everything they need to know to build statistical/machine learning models to find fraud in data events. We will cover the basics of building fraud models: understanding the problem dynamics, modes of fraud, data analysis, and preparation, building expert variables/features, different algorithm choices, and measurements of model goodness. Students will not receive credit for both MGTA 463 and MGTA 463R.
MGTA 463.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics students or instructor approval or department approval.

MGTA 463R.desc: In this course students will learn everything they need to know to build statistical/machine learning models to find fraud in data events. We will cover the basics of building fraud models: understanding the problem dynamics, modes of fraud, data analysis and preparation, building expert variables/features, different algorithm choices, and measurements of model goodness. Students will not receive credit for both MGTA 463R and MGTA 463. This is a distance education course.
MGTA 463R.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics students or instructor approval or department approval.

MGTA 464.desc: Most organizations store transaction data (e.g., sales, purchases, production, etc.) in relational databases. These databases are of central importance in most business analytics projects. To access and analyze this data, knowledge of SQL (structured query language), one of the most sought-after skills by recruiters, is needed. In this course, students will learn how to write SQL statements to extract and transform data. Students will be introduced to ETL (extract, transform, and load) concepts.
MGTA 464.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics students.

MGTA 466.desc: This course is designed to provide students with skills and knowledge to perform analytics at scale. Topics include steps in the analytics process used to gather, prepare, process, and evaluate data; basic principles of computer systems and parallelism; scalable computing; and cloud-based analytics. Hands-on experience with widely used scalable and cloud platforms will be provided. Through programming assignments, students will apply what they learn in the course to leverage big data.
MGTA 466.pre: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 479.desc: This class covers the key drivers for making data-driven pricing decisions. Price setting is one of the most crucial of all tactical marketing decisions. It involves a detailed understanding of both supply-side (e.g., costs) and demand-side factors (e.g., consumer willingness to pay). In this course, we will approach the pricing decision as an intersection of economic, strategic, and behavioral considerations.
MGTA 479.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

MGTA 495.desc: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in business analytics. Instructional methods can include face-to-face lecture, case presentations, assigned teaching and/or online group discussions.
MGTA 495.pre: restricted to MS in business analytics program or by department approval.
